title: An Ultrasonic Tool for Nerve Conduction Block in Diabetic Rat Models
protocol: Remove rat food pellets from the cage to fast male SD rats (300 - 350 g) for 6 hours prior to STZ induction.
Dissolve 1.05 g citric acid monohydrate in 50 mL distilled water to make a 0.1 M citric acid solution.
Dissolve 1.47 g trisodium citrate dihydrate in 50 mL distilled water to make a 0.1 M sodium citrate solution.
Add 25 mL of the citric acid solution to 25 mL of the sodium citrate solution.
Monitor the pH of the sodium citrate buffer (pH should be 4.5).
Dissolve STZ in 0.1 M sodium citrate buffer to yield a 50 mg/mL STZ solution.
Cover the STZ solution with aluminum foil and use within 15 - 20 minutes.
Draw the 50 mg/kg STZ solution into a 1 mL insulin or tuberculin syringe with a 26- to 28-gauge needle.
Clean the injection site with an ethanol pad.
Intraperitoneally inject the STZ solution into the lower right quadrant of the abdomen.
Supply rats with 10% sucrose water as the sole water source for 48 hours after STZ injection.
Monitor the fasting plasma glucose concentration of all rats injected by STZ post 72 h with a glucose meter.
Fast the STZ-induced diabetic rats for 15 h before measuring the fasting blood glucose level.
Restrain the rats in a restraint bag and expose the tails for blood collection during the blood glucose measurements.
Use a blood lancet to prick the tip of the tail to obtain a small drop of blood.
Place the drop of blood on a glucose test strip.
Record the fasting plasma glucose levels.
Exclude the rats with fasting blood glucose levels below 150 mg/dL after 2 weeks of STZ-induction.
Habituate the STZ-induced diabetic rats in a cage on a 1 cm diameter metal mesh floor for 30 min before evaluating the hind paw withdrawal response.

Use an electronic von Frey probe with rigid tip (0.8 mm in diameter) to manually apply pressure to the plantar surface of the hind paw of the rats, and gradually increase the pressure until a paw withdrawal response is seen.
Record the pressure that shows on the system and repeat the measurement 5 times per rat, with a 30 s interval between each measurement.
Assess the heat hyperalgesia with a hot plate.
Habituate the STZ-induced diabetic rats on the hot plate at 24 ± 0.5 °C for 10 min before evaluating pain response.
Remove and place the rats back into their cages after habituation.
Heat the hot plate and maintain its temperature at 55 ± 0.5 °C.
Place the rat on the heated hot plate while simultaneously starting the timer.
Stop the timer and record the withdrawal latency when the rat exhibits distinct behaviors such as licking the hind paw or abnormally flicking the hind paw.
Terminate the hot plate test if a rat does not express distinct behaviors after 20 s (20 s cut-off time).
Sterilize surgical tools in an autoclave before surgery.
Anesthetize the rats with intraperitoneal injection of tiletamine/zolazepam mixture and xylazine or via inhalation of 1.75% isoflurane.
Place the rats on a heating pad to maintain body temperature during anesthesia.
Position the rats for surgery in ventral recumbency.
Apply eye ointment to protect the eyes during surgery.
Extend the leg of the rat and pinch the plantar surface of the foot with fingernails to ascertain the depth of anesthesia.
Apply additional anesthesia if the rats show withdrawal responses.
Remove hair from the thigh and lower back of the rats with an electric clipper.
Apply liquid iodine with clean gauze at the surgical site in a circular motion.
Wipe the liquid iodine with an alcohol pad using the same circular motion.
Repeat the procedure on the other surgical site when performing subsequent steps.
Make an incision in the skin at the dorsal thigh using a sterile surgical scissors or scalpel.
Use blunt surgical scissors to carefully separate tissue underneath the skin and secure the skin with skin hooks.
Carefully separate the muscles parallel to the femur until the mid-thigh sciatic nerve fibers are visible.
Separate the mid-thigh sciatic nerve from surrounding connective tissues and muscles using a glass hook.
Position the sciatic nerve in the HIFU focal zone using a custom-made nerve fixator.
Construct component I with an external thread that is 2.5 mm tall and M10XP0.7.
Create a central well through component I, having a diameter of 4.0 mm.
Seal the bottom opening of the central well with a sheet of tape.
Design component II with four legs, including two short legs for alignment and two long legs for hooking onto component III.
Ensure the internal thread of the bottom structure in component II is 2.5 mm tall and M10XP0.7 to fit component I.
Make the diameter of the central hole in component II the same as the central well of component I.
Fabricate the main body of component II with dimensions of 32 mm in diameter and 5.4 mm in thickness.
Deploy four legs symmetrically on component II, ensuring two identical short legs for alignment and two long legs for hooking onto component III.
Design component III with an outer diameter of 41 mm and a height of 9.2 mm.
Incorporate an internal thread in component III that is M36XP1.0 to connect with component II.
Create a through hole in component III with a diameter of 27.5 mm.
Construct the cone as a hollow taper with the top opening at 84 mm in diameter and the bottom opening at 27.5 mm in diameter, with a height of 57.5 mm.
Soak the custom-made acrylic nerve fixator in bleach solution for 30 - 60 min.
Rinse the fixator in sterile water.
Lift the nerve carefully using a glass hook.
Place the nerve in the slot of component I.
Screw component II to component I.
Fill the central well of component I with Ringer's solution.
Screw component III to the HIFU housing cone.
Dock component III with component II through the four legs of component II.
Insert one pair of acupuncture needles into the origin of the sciatic nerve.
Insert another pair of acupuncture needles into the gastrocnemius muscle.
Connect each pair of needles to the electrophysiology acquisition system using an electrical coaxial cable.
Set the sampling rate and bandwidth of the electrophysiology acquisition system to 50 kHz and 70 Hz-3 kHz, respectively.
Apply a supra-maximal stimulus with a pulse width of 0.1 ms to the stimulating electrodes at the origin of the sciatic nerve.
Record CMAPs from the recording electrodes.
Amplify the CMAPs using the built-in amplifier in the electrophysiology acquisition system.
Immerse the spherical cone, HIFU transducer, and cone cover in a tank filled with degassed water.
Put the HIFU transducer into the spherical cone.
Fix the cone cover to the top opening of the spherical cone by 6 head screws.
Expel bubbles naturally from the spherical cone due to their low density compared to water.
Seal the front-end opening of the cone with a transparent 0.03 mm thick tape.
Screw component III onto the spherical cone.
Take out the HIFU transducer with the spherical cone and component III from the degassed water tank.
Put component I into the space between the nerve and the muscle carefully.
Position the nerve in the gap of component I.
Link a function generator to a radiofrequency power amplifier.
Connect the power amplifier to the HIFU transducer for generation of the HIFU beam.
Manually set the voltage output of the function generator to the HIFU transducer via the power amplifier.
Manually turn off the function generator once the HIFU-exposure time is up.
Simultaneously deliver the stimulus via the electrophysiology acquisition system and HIFU beam via HIFU system to the sciatic nerve while recording CMAPs.
Gradually increase the HIFU exposure on the sciatic nerve from 3 s, 5 s to 8 s until a decrease or inhibition of the amplitude of CMAPs is observed.
Record CMAPs once per second during the delivery of the HIFU beam.
Turn off the HIFU system when observing changes in CMAP amplitude.
Manually click on the record icon in the electrophysiology acquisition software.
Record CMAPs every 2 min for the first 10 min after sonication.
Switch to recording CMAPs every 5 min for the following 30 min.
Change to recording CMAPs every 10 min until reaching a total of 2 hours.
Separate component II and III of the nerve fixator to remove the HIFU transducer.
Release the secured sciatic nerve by separating component II and I.
Suture the surgical site with 4-0 chromic catgut sutures after recording CMAPs.
Apply liquid iodine to the surgical site to prevent infection.
Place the cages on a heating pad for rat recovery.
Return rats to their cages in the animal facility post-recovery.
Provide rats with ibuprofen in drinking water or intraperitoneal buprenorphine (0.05 - 0.1 mg/kg) for pain management.
Insert stimulating and recording electrodes at the origin of the sciatic nerve on days 7, 14, and 28 post-HIFU sonication.
Insert electrodes in the gastrocnemius muscles as described in steps 4.1.2 and 4.3.
Repeat steps 4.3.1 to 4.3.2 for subsequent measurements.
Place the rat in a carbon dioxide chamber.
Wait about 5 min for the rats to stop breathing.
Ensure that the heart has stopped beating.
